newsitem.title: MALI: Mali passes budget with deficit sharply down.
newsitem.headline: Mali passes budget with deficit sharply down.

text.p: Parliament approved Mali's 1997 budget totalling 779.8 billion CFA francs ($1.5 billion) with the deficit slashed by more than a half to 20.7 billion CFA.

Finance Minister Soumaila Cisse said on state television after the parliamentary vote on Monday that adoption of the finance law "showed recognition of the government's efforts at improving management of public finances".
The 1996 budget deficit was 46.4 billion CFA and the 1997 figure confirms a trend since 1994 to reduce the deficit.
"It would have been 13.6 billion were it not for spending related to the 1997 elections," Cisse said.
He said this was a result of curbs on overall spending that will increase by 5.27 percent in 1997 to 400.3 billion CFA, against 380.3 billion in 1996.
Revenue in 1997 is projected to improve by 13.7 percent to 379.5 billion CFA, compared with 333.8 billion CFA in 1996. About 203 billion CFA of the revenue is expected to be from government receipts.

The minister said the government would maintain its efforts at financial control to reach targeted Gross Domestic Product growth in the budget year of 5.1 percent and inflation at 3.0 percent. He gave no updated GDP or inflation figures for 1996.
